solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Maybe Glaswegian father evacuated estate without harm

parts.note: a Glaswegian is one example of a Scot, hence the 'Maybe'

indicators.note: an evacuated word has had its insides cleared out, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A Glasgow dad walks away unhurt after his housing estate is cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evacuated' works on both 'father' and 'estate', emptying each to its outer letters, FR and EE.
explanation.definitionFit: To get off scot-free is an idiom for escaping with no punishment or injury.

clue.text: Detective's hot meal

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, and with the 's it gives DIS
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A police inspector's spicy dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish is a prepared course of food, so it can stand for a meal.

clue.text: Fair-haired British duke in isolated environment

indicators.note: in places the duke's letter inside the word for isolated
an environment surrounds what lives in it, so the word for isolated wraps the duke's letter

parts.note: isolated means alone, lone

explanation.surface: A fair-haired British aristocrat living somewhere remote.
explanation.definitionFit: Blonde describes someone with pale yellow hair, a synonym for fair-haired.

clue.text: Poser troubled unknown raptor

indicators.note: troubled letters are disturbed and thrown into a new order

parts.note: Y is one of the algebraic unknowns, alongside x and z

explanation.surface: An awkward show-off encounters a mysterious bird of prey.
explanation.definitionFit: The osprey is a fish-eating bird of prey, and raptor is the general term for such birds.

clue.text: Muscle training on hill in California

parts.note: PE is physical education, school training

indicators.note: in places the hill's letters inside the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Building muscle by training on a Californian hill.
explanation.definitionFit: The pectoral is the chest muscle, so it is an example of a muscle.

clue.text: Body of seamen lifted vehicle with Yankee

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the word for vehicle is read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Sailors hoist a vehicle aboard alongside an American.
explanation.definitionFit: A navy is a nation's force of sailors and ships, an organised body of seamen.

clue.text: Classical hero to relax in sea to the west

indicators.note: in puts the word for relax inside the word for sea
in an across clue, going west means reading right to left, so the word sea is reversed

parts.note: taken as written
to chill is slang for to relax

explanation.surface: A legendary hero unwinding in the western sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the west' makes AES; in an across clue, west is leftward, so the word is read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles is the Greek warrior of the Iliad, a hero of classical myth.

clue.text: Greek character joins learner and others

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet
L is for learner, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A Greek person joins a trainee and some companions.
explanation.definitionFit: Et al. is the Latin abbreviation used in references to mean and others.

clue.text: English river's constant — woman following it

indicators.note: following tells us the constant and woman come after the word it

parts.note: taken as written
C is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
hen is a slang term for a woman, especially in Scotland

explanation.surface: A river described as faithful, with a woman following it along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constant' looks like a description of the river but is the letter C. The Itchen is a river in Hampshire, flowing through Winchester to Southampton.
explanation.definitionFit: The Itchen is a chalk stream in southern England, so it is an example of an English river.

clue.text: Raymond entertains non-drinker, irritable

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them inside, so the non-drinker goes within the name

parts.note: Ray is short for Raymond
TT means teetotal, a non-drinker

explanation.surface: Raymond hosts a teetotaller and is grumpy about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is British informal for bad-tempered, a synonym of irritable.

clue.text: Stain wood navy blue last of all

indicators.note: last of all asks for the final letter of every one of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: Instructions to finish by staining the wood navy blue.
explanation.definitionFit: To dye something is to colour it, and stain is a synonym for that colouring.

clue.text: Card game's deck controlled by captain

definitions.meaning: a card game played by two pairs
a ship's ... is the raised platform from which the captain commands

explanation.surface: A card game's pack is in the captain's hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' looks like a pack of cards, but here it is a level of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridge names both the partnership card game and the command platform of a ship.

clue.text: Supply food shop particularly

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a food shop
very means particularly, as in very good

explanation.surface: A food shop that is especially good at supplying.
explanation.definitionFit: Delivery is the act of supplying goods, so the noun supply fits it.

clue.text: Beam of light reflected terrace's herbal plant

indicators.note: a reflected image is reversed, so the word for the beam is read backwards

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light
a terrace is a row of joined houses

explanation.surface: Sunlight bounces off a terrace where herbs grow.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarrow is a feathery-leaved plant long used in herbal medicine.

clue.text: Running away, knight enters hotel abroad in the morning

indicators.note: enters puts the knight's letter inside the jumbled hotel
abroad suggests being all over the place, so the letters of hotel are rearranged

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight
AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

explanation.surface: A fugitive knight checks into a foreign hotel at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' rearranges HOTEL to OTHEL and 'enters' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: On the lam is American slang for fleeing, especially escaping the police.

clue.text: The German introduces beer merchant

indicators.note: introduces is read as the German word taking the beer inside it

parts.note: der is German for the
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A German presents a beer trader.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer is a trader in goods, a synonym for merchant.

clue.text: Posh car that might be stuck in Barnet

definitions.text: that might be stuck in Barnet
definitions.meaning: a hair curler; Barnet is rhyming slang for hair, from Barnet Fair

explanation.surface: A luxury car caught in traffic in the London suburb of Barnet.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet looks like the north London place, but in Cockney rhyming slang Barnet (Fair) means hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Roller is both slang for a Rolls-Royce and the word for a curler put in hair.

clue.text: Well-mannered cops, having time for Charlie

indicators.note: having time means the word for cops takes on a T, as part of a swap
for marks what is replaced: the time letter goes in where Charlie's letter was

parts.note: cops are the police
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Courteous officers who make time for a chap called Charlie.
explanation.definitionFit: Polite means showing good manners, a direct synonym of well-mannered.

clue.text: European group interrupting dad's ball game

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so these letters go inside the word for dad

parts.note: pa is dad; the 's is a link meaning is
a lot is a group, as in that lot

explanation.surface: A crowd of Europeans barges in on Dad's ball game.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelota is a Basque court game played by hitting a ball against a wall.

clue.text: Poem daughter's seen in Old English

indicators.note: seen in places the daughter's letter inside the abbreviation

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter; the 's means is

explanation.surface: A daughter's poem appears written in Old English.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem addressed to a subject, so it is a kind of poem.

clue.text: Block used by blacksmith in Asian village

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies within the letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A smithy's block found in a village in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: An anvil is the heavy iron block a blacksmith hammers metal on.

clue.text: Middle Eastern port, a retreat

parts.note: a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: A Middle Eastern harbour described as a place of refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: Aden is a port city in Yemen, at the mouth of the Red Sea.

clue.text: Dicky clear about new soldier

indicators.note: about means going round, so the jumbled letters surround the letter for new
dicky is British slang for unsound or faulty, so the letters of clear are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Dicky tidies up around a newcomer to the ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name but is the anagram indicator, giving LANCER minus N; 'about' places N inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A lancer is a cavalryman armed with a lance, a type of soldier.

clue.text: Spy initially navigates rescue boat

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letter of the word after it

parts.note: Noah's ark was the boat that rescued the animals from the Flood

explanation.surface: A secret agent steers a lifeboat at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Nark is British slang for a police informer, someone who spies and reports.

clue.text: Fruit couple heard of

indicators.note: heard of tells us to take how the word for couple sounds when spoken

parts.note: a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: A pair of people who have heard of some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The pear is a sweet tree fruit, so it is an example of fruit.

clue.text: Once seabird confronting Alan outside

parts.note: ex means former, once
a tern is a seabird
Al is short for Alan

explanation.surface: A former seabird squaring up to a man named Alan outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: External means on the outside, so it is a synonym of outside as an adjective.
